title: Beautiful, and Not
label: ch:ml-beauty
canDo: I can say that something is beautiful, name beauty itself, and deny it.

payoff.summary: From cold: both ends of one quality, and which letter arrives when aaNu follows a word.
payoff.note: WRITTEN FROM AN ENUMERATION RATHER THAN A GUESS, which is the correction taken from chapter 96's five review rounds. Before drafting, every attested quality-plus-aaNu form in the corpus was grepped: the welds are -am -> maaNu (sukhamaaNu, moshamaaNu, eLuppamaaNu), -i -> yaaNu (kuttiyaaNu) and -athu -> thaaNu (nallathaaNu). The chapter teaches the first two and says only what that enumeration supports -- a letter ARRIVES to carry aaNu's vowel, and which one depends on how the word ended. Nothing is claimed about a third case the lessons do not show. NO DEDICATED WORD FOR 'UGLY' IS TAUGHT: vrtthiketta would need an attributive form and a register judgement that could not be defended under review, so the far end of the axis is built with alla, which ML-C77 teaches STANDING APART (njaan adhyaapakan alla) -- and the lesson makes the not-welding the point, since sundaram keeps its anusvara precisely because nothing attached.
